bull.b: Arm’s licensing and royalty model supports exceptional gross margins while producing substantial operating and free cash flow. This combination gives the company capacity to fund research, expand its technology portfolio, and pursue AI-related opportunities without relying heavily on external financing.

Rapid growth in data-center royalties and expanding Neoverse shipments indicate that Arm is gaining durable share in infrastructure computing. Broader use across servers and AI systems can diversify the business beyond smartphones and increase recurring royalty opportunities as customer chips enter production.

bull.t: Strong AGI CPU demand and ecosystem reach
bull.b: Demand exceeding Arm’s original AGI CPU target demonstrates meaningful customer traction for a new, higher-value platform. Combined with major cloud partnerships and a large developer ecosystem, this may strengthen adoption, accelerate design wins, and extend Arm’s strategic relevance in AI infrastructure.

bear.b: Smartphone weakness remains a fundamental exposure because handset royalties are tied to customer chip shipments and device volumes. Higher memory-driven bill-of-materials costs can pressure demand and product mix, limiting royalty growth even as Arm expands into data centers and AI.

bear.t: Supply constraints may limit AGI CPU scaling
bear.b: The AGI CPU opportunity depends on customers obtaining sufficient wafer, substrate, testing, and memory capacity. These constraints can delay production ramps and royalty-bearing shipments, limiting near- to medium-term monetization even though customer demand and the opportunity pipeline are strong.

bear.t: Initial AGI CPU margins are below long-term goals
bear.b: The initial AGI CPU margin profile is materially below Arm’s established IP economics and its longer-term target. Lower early margins could dilute consolidated profitability as the product scales, while the expected improvement depends on execution, volume, and platform maturation over multiple years.
